newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks surge to new intraday record.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks surge to new intraday record.

text.p: Mexican stocks shook off their early indecision and advanced to a new trading record shortly before mid-session on Friday.
Dealers said share prices had gained as a soaring Dow Jones Industrial Average in the United States put an end to recent profit-taking and brought back foreign and local buyers to the Mexican market.
The leading IPC share index .MXX was up 25.70 points, or 0.62 percent, at 4,145.23.
The Dow Jones had meanwhile gained 102.59 points to 7,407.88.

"The Dow obviously helps, there's no other fresh news. Heavyweights like Telmex and ICA are driving the bourse. Also, confidence in Mexico is high, and the market is still reacting favorably to the Pronafide," a desk trader said.
Mexico's President Zedillo announced the National Development Financing program (Pronafide) on Tuesday.
Telecomms firm Telmex, up 14 centavos to 18.64 pesos, was the mostly heavily traded stock in normal dealing, without counting cross trades.
Telmex ADRs were meanwhile up 5/8 to 46-7/8.
Shares listed by construction firm ICA had gained 5.20 pesos to 118.70 pesos.
Trading volume .TV.MX was brisk, despite being inflated by cross trades, at 74.2 million shares.

Retail stock Cifra B shares were high on the prominent sliders' list .PL.MX, down 30 centavos to 13.30 pesos, having shed gains previously notched up on unfounded speculation the firm was to sell holdings to Wal-Mart Stores Inc, dealers said.
